prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Conroe, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1372; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision at the intersection in Conroe, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd prefer to leave my name out of the recording, but I can confirm I was the driver of my vehicle that day.

Q: That's fine. Can you walk me through what happened before the collision?

A: I was heading through the intersection on a green light. I'd slowed down a bit because traffic was backed up on the cross street, but I had the right of way.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?

A: Not really. It came from my right side, and I only caught a glimpse of it right before it hit my driver's side door.

Q: Where were you hurt?

A: My left wrist took the worst of it. I put my hand up on the steering wheel and the airbag went off. I got checked at the emergency room, and they said the wrist is fractured. I've got a splint on it now and I'm waiting on a follow-up with an orthopedic specialist.

Q: Were you able to get out of the vehicle on your own?

A: Yes, I got out, but it was painful and I felt dizzy for a while. Someone nearby helped me sit down until the ambulance arrived.

Q: Did you receive any treatment besides the emergency room?

A: Not yet. I've been taking the pain medication they prescribed and icing the wrist at home.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you think I should know about the incident?

A: Only that I'm worried about how long I'll be out of work, since I use my left hand a lot on the job.

Q: Understood. Thank you for your cooperation today.

A: You're welcome.
